item.title: Preventing not assisting suicide
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor “Assisted dying”, in the sense of supplying lethal drugs to enable someone who has a terminal illness to take their own life, is not a death from natural causes, but is a death by a person’s own hand. Baroness Hayter and others[1] take issue with the term “assisted suicide” in this context. item.title: Antidepressant exposure should be considered when interpreting youth suicide trends
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor Padmanathan and colleagues describe rising youth suicide rates and discuss a range of social and population-level factors that may contribute to these trends.[1] One additional factor that may be relevant, but is not mentioned, is adolescent antidepressant use. item.title: Heterogeneous Responses to Knee Bracing in Osteoarthritis: Insights from the PROP OA Trial
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, The PROP OA trial[1] found that compartment-specific bracing with adherence support (AIE+B) led to statistically significant but modest KOOS-5 improvements over AIE alone at six months in knee OA, with a favorable safety profile. item.title: Artificial intelligence, bibliometric ethics, and the need for practical wisdom
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor Until recently, using bibliometric methods to solve issues of publication ethics (1) relied on a ‘low-tech’ approach involving repetitive human labour in samples of dozens or hundreds of articles. item.title: How people leave public service matters
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Ministers talk at length about duplication of bureaucracy and organisational design, with little regard to the people asked to leave and why this matters. item.title: Re: The UK’s recruitment for foundation medicine requires radical reform
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor I am a current FY2 doctor who was part of the first cohort of doctors who were allocated their foundation job based on this random allocation system and I am unsure if the changes announced to prioritise UK graduates is enough progress.
